function: Robust downlink beamforming: a liquid neural network fed with objective gradients updates a low-dimensional base matrix of the precoder to maximize weighted sum spectral efficiency. p. 1
system: Downlink mmWave massive MU-MIMO: BS with M=64 antennas, K=4 users with Nk=2 antennas each, fc=28 GHz, DeepMIMO O1 scenario with BS3; no RIS. p. 4
method: Gradient-based liquid neural network (ODE-based neurons, residual update) on a manifold-compressed precoder; unsupervised online learning with loss -R plus penalty and incentive terms, Adam, 500-sample warm-up. p. 4
data_channel: DeepMIMO open dataset, scenario O1, BS3, M=64, Nk=2, K=4, 28 GHz; 500 samples with continuously changing positions; estimation error modeled as white Gaussian. p. 4
test_conditions: Warm-up of 500 samples, then 500 moving-user samples; CEE swept -20 to 0 dB; dynamic test without warm-up at speeds 6, 15, 30 m/s in successive phases. p. 4
baselines: Classical: WMMSE iterative algorithm [20]. Learned: LAGD [9] and an LSTM mapping the estimated channel to the precoder; upper bound is the best of 100 runs. p. 4
metrics: Spectral efficiency versus transmit power, channel estimation error (CEE), and time slots under mobility; CPU time per sample versus number of BS antennas M. p. 4-5
complexity: Total complexity O(Ne(MNK+M^2K+Nk^3)) (Table I, p. 5); CPU time per sample versus M in Fig. 6, with GLNN at 1.61% of WMMSE time at M=160.
openness: Code released at https://github.com/tp1000d/GLNN (reference [15], p. 5); channels from the open DeepMIMO dataset. p. 2
q1_support: p. 4: "We construct the channel matrix using BS3 from scenario O1 of the open source DeepMIMO dataset [19]".
q2_support: p. 4: "We provide three phases of speed, including 6 m/s, 15 m/s, and 30 m/s", run without warm-up; p. 5: "just a few iterations, demonstrating its high adaptability" after the speed changes.
q3_support: p. 4: "Baseline 1 (WMMSE): An iterative scheme from [20]" and "Baseline 2 (LAGD): A DL-based model from [9]", plus an LSTM baseline, all compared on SE in Figs. 3-5.
q4_support: p. 5: "the total complexity of GLNN is O(Ne (MNK + M 2 K + Nk3 ))"; Table I and Fig. 6 (CPU time per sample) also report cost.
q5_support: p. 2: "we have made our work open source at [15]"; reference [15] on p. 5 gives "https://github.com/" followed by "tp1000d/GLNN".
notes: Area 3: the learned GLNN designs the BS precoder, and the letter has no RIS (RIS appears only in cited works [8], [11]). The q2 mark rests on the Fig. 5 phases (6, 15, 30 m/s) and the reported adaptation in a few iterations; GLNN learns online after a 500-sample warm-up, with no separate offline training set, so the reviewer should confirm it. Table I and the figures were read from the page images (pp. 4-5). The title and DOI on p. 1 match the work.
